degree: BS in Statistics and Machine Learning (Dietrich College) + Additional Major in Robotics (Robotics Institute)
assumption: B grades in the required courses, as specified.
note: Every course code, prerequisite and Fall/Spring offering above comes from the CMU course catalog. Dietrich general-education requirements were not researched, so they appear as labelled placeholders rather than invented courses, each estimated at 9 units.
fulltime_rule: Students are considered full time if registered for 36 or more units.
registration_rule: In order to ensure that students do not have to compete for access to their required courses, registration priority is given to students who are registering for courses in their primary major. Although the university encourages the exploration of other disciplines, access to courses outside a student's primary major (including those courses that fulfill requirements for an additional major, minor, etc.) is on a space-available basis and is not guaranteed.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Programming and Computer Science
courses.note: The gateway. Everything downstream depends on it.

courses.title: Dietrich general education / first-year writing
courses.note: Dietrich's gen-ed requirements were not researched — confirm with an advisor.

semesters.why: Nothing robotics-specific yet. The only job this semester has is to get 15-112 done, because it unlocks the entire chain.

courses.title: Principles of Imperative Computation
courses.note: Prereq 15-112 (min C). This is the single most load-bearing course in the plan.

courses.title: Integration and Approximation
courses.note: Not strictly required by the major, but 16-299 controls requires it. Take it now.

courses.title: General Robotics
courses.note: Spring only. Prereq is just 15-112 (min C), so this is the EARLIEST possible robotics entry — and it is one of the two courses 16-450 later requires.

semesters.why: 16-281 lands in the first year purely because it is Spring-only and gates 16-450 three years later. Getting it early also means declaring the Additional Major early, which matters for registration priority.

courses.title: Matrices and Linear Transformations
courses.note: Prereq for 10-301, 16-384, 16-385 and 16-421. Second most load-bearing course here.

courses.title: Statistical Computing
courses.note: Placed early so that a robotics elective can sit in Year 3 Spring instead.

semesters.why: A maths-heavy semester on purpose: 21-241 has to be finished before 10-301 and the whole perception line opens up.

courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.note: CMU states 10-301 'is recommended for undergraduates who are not SCS majors' — this is the version open to him, not 10-315.

courses.title: Introduction to Feedback Control Systems
courses.note: Spring only. Prereqs 15-122 and 21-122, both already done. 16-450 needs a minimum grade of B here — taking it now leaves a full year to retake if the grade comes in at B-minus.

semesters.why: The pivotal semester. Controls is deliberately two years before it is needed, because it is the one course where a B-minus would collapse the robotics credential.

courses.title: Robot Kinematics and Dynamics
courses.note: Fall only. Prereq satisfied by 21-241 or 15-122.

courses.title: Algorithms and Advanced Data Structures
courses.note: The non-SCS algorithms route; 15-451 is the SCS version.

semesters.why: Statistics core and the mechanics half of robotics run in parallel. No Spring-only course is at risk here.

courses.title: Introduction to Robot Learning
courses.note: The tenth robotics course, filling the second elective slot. Runs Fall and Spring with no published prerequisites, and pairs naturally with 10-403 the same semester.

courses.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning & Control
courses.note: Spring only. Prereq 10-301, already done. This single course is the best learning-plus-control bridge in the catalog and it fills the major's required ML Advanced Elective slot.

courses.title: Planning Techniques for Robotics
courses.note: Spring only. No published prerequisites.

semesters.why: The AI half gets its depth here. 10-403 does double duty — it satisfies a required major slot and counts as robotics-relevant learning.

courses.title: Robotics Systems Engineering
courses.note: Fall only, and the hard gate: requires (16-281 or 16-280) AND a minimum grade of B in 16-299. Both are behind him by now.

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.note: Fills the sensing/perception requirement. CMU notes 'This course is for undergraduate students only.'

courses.title: Mobile Robot Algorithms Laboratory
courses.note: Fall only. Chosen as the hands-on requirement because it publishes no prerequisites — 16-220 Robot Building Practices would additionally require a physics course the major does not include.

semesters.why: Three Fall-only robotics courses land together here, which is unavoidable — 16-450 and 16-362 run in Fall only, and 16-385 has to precede the capstone. At 36 units this is exactly full-time with no room spare, so no elective is placed alongside them.

courses.title: Robotics Capstone
courses.note: Spring only. Prereq 16-450 (min C). This is the portfolio piece employers will actually ask about.

courses.title: Advanced Data Analysis elective (36-xxx)
courses.note: Both 36-xxx advanced electives sit here because they require 36-401 and 36-402 first.

courses.title: Ethics requirement for the Additional Major in Robotics
courses.note: The Robotics curriculum includes an ethics requirement; the approved list was not captured in research — confirm the options with the Robotics Institute.

semesters.why: Capstone semester. Everything else is deliberately light so the capstone gets real time.

risks.risk: A straight-B average sits exactly on the 3.0 line — twice
risks.detail: The Additional Major in Robotics requires a 3.0 GPA to apply and 'a minimum 3.0 QPA in the Additional Major curriculum is required for graduation'. Straight B is exactly 3.00, so a single B-minus in any of the ten robotics courses puts the credential below the graduation threshold. This is the tightest constraint in the whole plan.
risks.mitigation: Treat the robotics courses as the ones to over-perform in, not the statistics core. The statistics core has no QPA gate attached to it; the robotics curriculum does.

risks.risk: 16-450 requires a minimum grade of B, not a pass
risks.detail: Its prerequisites are '(16-311 Min. grade B or 16-280 or 16-281) and (16-299 Min. grade B or 18-370 Min. grade B or 24-451 Min. grade B)'. A B-minus in 16-299 blocks 16-450, which blocks 16-474, which ends the Additional Major.
risks.mitigation: This is why 16-299 sits in Year 2 Spring rather than Year 3. Because 16-299 is Spring-only and 16-450 is Fall-only, taking controls in Year 2 leaves a full extra Spring to retake it and still reach 16-450 on time. Taking it in Year 3 removes that buffer entirely.

risks.risk: None of these robotics seats are guaranteed to him
risks.detail: In order to ensure that students do not have to compete for access to their required courses, registration priority is given to students who are registering for courses in their primary major. Although the university encourages the exploration of other disciplines, access to courses outside a student's primary major (including those courses that fulfill requirements for an additional major, minor, etc.) is on a space-available basis and is not guaranteed.
risks.mitigation: Declare the Additional Major as early as the 3.0 permits — 16-299's own description says priority goes to computer science majors with a robotics major or minor, so the declaration is what moves him into the named priority group. Ask about seat availability on the Pittsburgh visit; it is already on his question list.

risks.risk: Year 4 Fall is three robotics project courses at once
risks.detail: 16-450, 16-362 and 16-385 total 36 units in a single semester — exactly full-time with nothing spare, and all three are demanding project courses. CMU sets normal load per department and permits an overload of up to 12 units only with advisor approval.
risks.mitigation: Already partly mitigated by placing no elective alongside them. If it still looks heavy when he gets there, 16-385 Computer Vision runs in both Fall and Spring, so it is the one shiftable course in the robotics set and can move to Year 3 Spring.

risks.detail: 16-385 is on both the major's ML Advanced Elective list and the robotics sensing requirement, and 10-403 is similarly dual-purpose. CMU's concentration rules elsewhere mention a minimum of non-double-counted units, but no double-counting rule for this specific pairing was found.
risks.mitigation: Ask the Statistics advisor before relying on any course to satisfy two requirements.

fallback.name: Minor in Robotics
fallback.why: If the B grades slip, this is the retreat. It requires 'a minimum 2.5 QPA in the Minor curriculum' rather than 3.0, and it does not require 16-450 or 16-474 — so it survives exactly the failure that would end the Additional Major.
fallback.cost: Minors are transcript-only: 'Minors are not listed on a diploma, although they do appear on an official transcript.' The Additional Major does appear on the diploma. That difference is the reason to aim for the Additional Major first.
fallback.also: The Minor in Machine Learning requires only a C or better in every course, so it is safe under a straight-B assumption and is worth holding as a guaranteed-looking credential either way.
